name: GetMentions AI
tagline: Paid brand mention and link placements across a large publisher network, pitched at getting your brand cited in AI search answers.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software here is the thin part: a dashboard, a prompt tracker, some reporting. The product you are actually buying is a rolodex of publishers who will accept a placement and an operations team that gets the piece live. No coding agent can generate an editor at a site with real traffic who says yes to your link. You can absolutely one-shot the measurement half, checking whether your brand shows up when models are asked buying-intent questions, and that is genuinely useful, but it tells you the problem rather than fixing it. The closest honest DIY is a visibility tracker plus an outreach CRM you then have to work by hand.
coreLoopDIY: Runs a saved list of buying-intent prompts against LLM APIs on a schedule, records whether your brand or domain gets mentioned, and tracks your own manual publisher outreach in the same local database.
requirements: An LLM API key or two, and budget for repeated queries
A list of prompts your buyers would actually type
Willingness to do outreach and negotiation yourself
Optional: a search API key if you want to cross-check cited sources
whatYouLose: The publisher network itself, which is the entire product
Someone else handling pitching, negotiation, and getting the piece actually published
Editorial vetting so your brand does not end up on obvious link farms
Volume: dozens of placements a month instead of you emailing three editors and hearing back from none
Client-ready reporting that ties placements to visibility changes
moatNotes: Supply side is the scarce good. Publishers who accept placements and still have traffic are a finite, relationship-gated list, and they get farmed out over time.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because measurement is cheap and distribution is not. Anyone can build a script that tells them ChatGPT never mentions their brand; almost nobody can build the list of sites that will publish something about them next week. Agencies pay for throughput and for not having to run a cold email operation, and they pay again for the plausible reporting they can forward to a client. If the placements are real and indexed, the price is basically arbitrage on relationships you do not have.
notes: You can one-shot the scoreboard, not the game. The moat is a supply side of publishers willing to run placements, and every one of those relationships was earned by a human on a phone.
prompt:
Build a local AI search visibility tracker and outreach log. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Python 3.11, plain venv, no Docker
- SQLite via sqlite3 stdlib, single file data/visibility.db
- typer for the CLI, httpx for API calls, jinja2 for the HTML report
- Secrets in .env loaded with python-dotenv: OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (either may be absent, skip that provider)

Data model:
- brands(id, name, domain, aliases_csv)
- prompts(id, brand_id, text, intent_tag)
- runs(id, prompt_id, provider, model, created_at, response_text, mentioned_bool, position_int, competitors_csv)
- prospects(id, brand_id, site_domain, contact, status, price_quoted, last_touch_at, notes)

Commands:
- init: create db and schema
- brand add / prompt add / prompt import from a CSV file
- run --brand X: send every prompt to each configured provider, store raw response, detect mentions of the brand name, aliases, or bare domain case-insensitively, record first-mention character offset as position, and extract other capitalized brand-like tokens into competitors_csv with a crude regex plus a stopword list
- report --brand X: write out/report.html with mention rate per prompt over time, a sparkline-free simple table, provider breakdown, and a top-competitors count
- prospect add / prospect touch --status: manual outreach log, no sending, no scraping

Rules:
- Sequential requests with a 1 second sleep, retry once on 429, print estimated call count and ask for confirmation before a run
- Never fabricate a result: if a provider call fails, store nothing for that pair and log it
- Deterministic settings: temperature 0, pinned model names in config.py

Out of scope, do not build: sending email, scraping publisher sites, buying placements, any hosted dashboard, auth, multi-user.

Deliver: README with setup in five commands, a seed CSV of ten example prompts, and pytest tests for mention detection including the alias and substring-false-positive cases.
